title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S is a scheme and Omega a locally free O_S-module (presumably Omega^1 of a relative curve or family). There is an extension 0 -> Omega -> E -> O_S -> 0. P = P(E) is the bundle of invertible quotients of E. The given quotient p : E -> O_S defines a section sigma. P^ is the formal completion of P along sigma, S^ = O_{P^}, and L^ is the completion of O_P(1). The additive group Omega acts on the extension, hence on (P, sigma), P^, S^ and L^.

Split case, E = Omega (+) O_S. Points of P^ near sigma are quotients (x, lambda) -> phi(x) + lambda, with phi : Omega -> nilradical. So P^ = V(Omega)^ = Spf Sym^(Omega), the completion of the vector bundle along its zero section. For a in Omega(S), u_a(x, lambda) = (x + lambda a, lambda) sends the quotient phi to phi^a = phi/(1 + phi(a)).

This page:
1. The transposed action on V(Omega)^ is phi -> phi/(1 + phi(a)). This is the unipotent group of projective transformations fixing a point with trivial differential, x -> x/(1 + <x, a>).
2. Dually, on functions it is the continuous ring automorphism u_{a*} of S^ = Sym^(Omega) given by u_{a*}(omega) = omega/(1 + a) = sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n omega a^n. Since 1 + a is a unit in the completion, u_{a*}(f) = f/(1 + a)^n for f homogeneous of degree n.
3. The tautological epimorphism E (x) S^ -> L^, with L^ trivialized as S^, is pi(omega (x) f, g) = omega f + g. Its restriction to the S^ summand is the identity; on Omega it is the inclusion Omega -> S^+.
4. The page then starts computing the action of u_a on L^ by first lifting it to E (x) S^.

The next page finishes this: u^L_{a*}(g) = (1 + a) u_{a*}(g), i.e. g/(1 + a)^{n-1} in degree n. In general, with E given by an Omega-torsor T, S^ and L^ are the contracted products T ^Omega Sym^(Omega) for the two actions.

Purpose: an explicit local model of the formal neighbourhood of the section in P(E) for a non-split extension (e.g. jet or Atiyah-type extensions). This is the formal structure of a projective bundle near a section, which is what projective connections / uniformization need.
errors: No mathematical errors. u_{a*} is a group action: u_b(omega/(1+a)) = omega/(1+a+b), so u_a u_b = u_{a+b}. The L^ action (1+a)u_{a*} satisfies the same cocycle identity.
The left/right bookkeeping ('transposé', u_a^t, action 'à droite' on P^) is only sketched. One must check u_{a*} versus u_{-a*} conventions, but this does not affect the formulas.
The crossed-out line 'phi(omega/(1+a)) =' is abandoned; the correct rewriting phi^a(omega) = phi(u_{a*} omega) follows it.

ideas.what: Formal completion of P(E) along the section given by the quotient E -> O_S, for an extension of O_S by Omega, identified with V(Omega)^ = Spf Sym^(Omega) in the split case and with a torsor-twist in general
ideas.modern_name: formal neighbourhood of a section of a projective bundle; twisted forms of formal affine space; linearizability of formal neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / formal-neighbourhood theory (Grauert, Griffiths, Hironaka–Matsumura style); jet/Atiyah-extension constructions

ideas.what: Action of Omega by fractional-linear automorphisms: omega -> omega/(1+a) on Sym^(Omega), and on O(1) by g -> (1+a) u_{a*}(g)
ideas.modern_name: unipotent radical of the stabilizer of a point in PGL (the 'special projective/conformal' transformations x -> x/(1+<a,x>)) acting on the formal neighbourhood and its O(1)

ideas.what: Explicit tautological surjection E (x) S^ -> L^, pi(omega (x) f, g) = omega f + g
ideas.modern_name: Euler/tautological quotient on P(E) restricted to the formal neighbourhood
ideas.where_published: EGA II §4 for P(E) in general

missed.claim: The page is part of a programme (completed on the next page) that describes the formal neighbourhood of the canonical section of P(E) for an arbitrary extension class in H^1(S, Omega). It does so as a contracted product of the class's Omega-torsor with Sym^(Omega), under a nonlinear (fractional-linear) action. In the notes' context, this presumably links the extension class (e.g. of a jet bundle) to the non-linearizability of the formal neighbourhood and to projective connections. The final passage from these local formulas to projective connections/uniformization is not on this page.
missed.quote: Quel est l'endomorphisme de L^ ≃ S^ induit par l'automorphisme u_a de la situation ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean, characteristic-free, scheme-theoretic description of formal neighbourhoods of sections in projective bundles twisted by torsors. It is relevant to opers/projective structures in positive or mixed characteristic. But the content itself is essentially standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are correct, routine explicit formulas: fractional-linear action of the vector group on Spf Sym^(Omega) and on O(1). They serve a torsor-twist description of a formal neighbourhood. This is careful bookkeeping toward projective connections rather than a new result.
